summary: Iteration 40 — Frontend-only run at 390x844 against the preview URL. HIGGINS 'Suggests' FLOW: core spec passes. Tapping Higgins tab, sending the AnyDesk scam prompt streams a Gemini reply in 10–20s whose visible text contains NO raw 'CHECKS:' trailer, names checks by their exact names ('Check my device', 'Check a message', 'Check a link', 'Check this app'), and renders the block testID `higgins-checks-a-<msgId>` with chips `higgins-check-{device|message|link|app}` and the progress line `higgins-checks-progress-<msgId>` = '0 of N done'. A plain question ('Should I run a check on this app I just installed?') returned exactly one chip (`higgins-check-app`). Tapping a chip navigates to the correct route (`/app-check`); after filling the App name and tapping `app-run`, returning to the Ask tab shows the chip visibly ticked, testID `higgins-check-app-done` appears, and the progress line becomes 'Done — thank you.'. Full page RELOAD correctly re-fetches history (1 apollo bubble) from `/api/ask/history` and, because `checkCompletion` is persisted to storage under `apollo.checks.completed.v1`, the Done state and 'Done — thank you.' progress persist. Onboarding 'APOLLO' eyebrow contrast is now fixed: color rgb(27,107,71) (#1B6B47) on rgb(230,240,250) = ~5.82:1 (>4.5). Resting-state pills ('Active', 'Patrolling', 'All good' equivalents) render text rgb(27,107,71) on rgba(79,175,131,0.20) composited over white = rgb(220,239,230), ratio ~5.47:1 (>4.5). CRITICAL FUNCTIONAL GAP FOUND: `markCheckDone()` is imported/called in ONLY 4 of 6 check screens — account.tsx, app-check.tsx, device.tsx, network.tsx. It is MISSING in message.tsx and check.tsx, so the `higgins-check-message` and `higgins-check-link` chips will never tick 'Done' even after the user actually runs those checks. Since the two most common suggestions Higgins emits for a scam-text prompt are exactly 'message' and 'link', this is a high-priority miss. SECONDARY-BUTTON CONTRAST FINDING: 'Add a screenshot of the page' on /check (test id `check-page-screenshot`) — a real `Button variant='secondary'` — is now white rgb(255,255,255) with navy border rgb(22,34,53) 1px and navy label rgb(22,34,53) as spec'd. BUT the 'Hear Higgins' button on Home and inside every Ask reply is NOT the shared Button component — it's `HigginsSpeakButton` (src/components/HigginsSpeakButton.tsx L12) with its own inline style `backgroundColor: c.surfaceTertiary` (#D9E7F5, i.e. rgb(217,231,245)) and `borderColor: c.border` (#C9D9EA, i.e. rgb(201,217,234), NOT navy). Computed on the running site: bg rgb(217,231,245), border rgb(201,217,234) 1px, text rgb(11,18,32). This blends into the sky-blue page (231≈surface(230)) — exactly the failure mode the request called out. The redesign missed this button. Danger button (event-block-button) could not be exercised because the /check submit for `https://phishing.apollo.test/login` did not produce a barking result card in this session (page cleared the input; the barking-result branch could not be re-created). The Button 'danger' palette in ui.tsx L118 uses `colors.barkingText` (#B3261E) as bg with `colors.onError` (#FFFFFF) as fg → 6.86:1 which meets the spec's 'expect ≥ 6:1'. Console warning observed (non-blocking): 'Each child in a list should have a unique key prop' from a VirtualizedList — likely `HigginsChecks` when the checks array is empty for a bubble and React sees the same non-keyed spacer, or in the ask.tsx FlatList when parseChecks strips CHECKS: mid-stream. Worth a quick review but no visible regression.

ui_bugs.issue: Uses its own inline style `backgroundColor: c.surfaceTertiary` (#D9E7F5) + `borderColor: c.border` (#C9D9EA) — visually blends into the sky-blue page (#E6F0FA). Spec required white bg rgb(255,255,255) + navy border rgb(22,34,53) + navy label. Fix: change `btn` style in /app/frontend/src/components/HigginsSpeakButton.tsx:12 to `backgroundColor: c.surfaceSecondary` (#FFFFFF) and `borderColor: c.brand` (#162235); the label already uses c.onSurface (navy) so no other change needed.
ui_bugs.testID: n/a (HigginsSpeakButton has no default testID; ask-hear-<id> and home Hear-Higgins have their own)

integration_issues.flow: Higgins 'Done' completion tracking for message/link checks
integration_issues.issue: markCheckDone() is NOT called in /app/frontend/app/message.tsx or /app/frontend/app/check.tsx. When Higgins suggests 'Check a message' or 'Check a link' (the two most common suggestions for a scam-text prompt), the user can run the check but the chip will NEVER show 'Done' and the progress line will never advance. Only device/app/account/network chips work. Fix: after a successful run in message.tsx (around L106 `run()` post-analyse) call `void markCheckDone('message')`; same in check.tsx after a successful reputation check, call `void markCheckDone('link')`. Verified against the sibling implementations in device.tsx L56, app-check.tsx L73, account.tsx L73, network.tsx L72.

issues: Could not exercise event-block-button in this run because /check submit for https://phishing.apollo.test/login did not render the barking result card (the URL field cleared or the mock adapter did not treat the domain as phishing on this route; needs a re-run or clarification on which URL triggers barking in web-preview MockSecurityAdapter). Token-level check: Button variant='danger' bg = colors.barkingText (#B3261E) on white text = 6.86:1 which meets the ≥6:1 spec — but this was not visually confirmed. Recommend main agent verify with an alternative barking scenario or expose event-block-button in a happy-path fixture.

react_native_issues.issue: Console warning: 'Each child in a list should have a unique key prop. Check the render method of View. It was passed a child from VirtualizedList.' — appeared twice this session while streaming/rendering ask messages with chip blocks. Reference: /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/ask.tsx around L90-96 renderItem and /app/frontend/src/components/HigginsChecks.tsx L32-41 chip .map (chips use `key={c}` which is correct, so the culprit is likely the conditional siblings inside the bubble View at ask.tsx L92-94 — three sibling nodes without keys inside a parent that RN Web is treating as a VirtualizedList child). Non-blocking but worth a review.

action_items: HIGH — Add `markCheckDone('message')` inside the successful path of message.tsx `run()` (after setResult / setBusy) so the `higgins-check-message` chip actually goes to Done. Model on device.tsx L56 or app-check.tsx L73.

HIGH — Add `markCheckDone('link')` inside the successful path of check.tsx after a reputation check completes so the `higgins-check-link` chip actually goes to Done. Without these two, roughly half of Higgins' suggested checks are dead-ends for the completion UI.

HIGH — Update HigginsSpeakButton style (src/components/HigginsSpeakButton.tsx L12): backgroundColor `c.surfaceTertiary` → `c.surfaceSecondary` (white), borderColor `c.border` → `c.brand` (navy). Keeps navy label. This is the 'Hear Higgins' button on Home and inside every Ask reply; it currently reads as bg rgb(217,231,245) / border rgb(201,217,234) on the sky-blue page rgb(230,240,250) — 1 shade of blue against another shade of blue. The Button variant='secondary' redesign already landed correctly (verified via check-page-screenshot 'Add a screenshot of the page'), it's only HigginsSpeakButton that was missed.

MEDIUM — Investigate the 'unique key prop' console warning: it fires from ask.tsx renderItem or HigginsChecks. Likely fix is wrapping the three conditional siblings (Text/HigginsChecks/HigginsSpeakButton) inside a keyed Fragment or explicit View children with keys.

LOW — Re-verify the danger button contrast (event-block-button) with a URL that reliably barks in web-preview MockSecurityAdapter, or provide a fixture that exposes the barking result card so the visual contrast can be measured (token-level maths at #B3261E on white = 6.86:1 clears the ≥6:1 bar; visual confirmation still pending).
critical_code_review_comments: src/components/HigginsSpeakButton.tsx L12 hard-codes `backgroundColor: c.surfaceTertiary` and `borderColor: c.border`. The whole point of the iteration-40 secondary-button redesign was to make Hear Higgins etc distinguishable from the sky-blue page — this component is the primary offender because it's the button 'Hear Higgins' referenced in the acceptance criteria. All other secondary CTAs correctly go through `Button variant='secondary'` in ui.tsx L116 which was correctly updated to `bg: colors.surfaceSecondary, fg: colors.brand, border: colors.brand`.

app/message.tsx and app/check.tsx are the ONLY check screens that don't import markCheckDone (grep across app/*.tsx confirms account, app-check, device, network all do). The Higgins→check→Done contract is silently broken for exactly the two check ids ('message', 'link') that Higgins recommends most often for scam-text prompts. This is a functional regression, not a design nit.

ask.tsx L52 initialises messages from history.data only when messages.length===0 — this is fine for the first mount but re-mounts (e.g. tab-switch) will not re-hydrate if the local list has already been populated. Not a bug for the reload path (verified: history rehydrates after full reload) but worth noting.
domain/higginsChecks.ts parseChecks() is invoked twice per apollo bubble render (once for text, once for checks) — trivial CPU, but easy win: memoise into a single call at renderItem level.

success_rate.frontend: Higgins chip suggestion flow: PASS for text-strip + naming + chips + navigation + persistence (via app-check path). FAIL for message/link Done tracking (markCheckDone missing). Secondary button redesign: PASS for Button variant='secondary' (Add a screenshot of the page → white bg + navy border + navy label), FAIL for HigginsSpeakButton (still surfaceTertiary + border). Contrast fixes: PASS onboarding APOLLO eyebrow (5.82:1), PASS resting pills (5.47:1). Danger button: token maths PASS 6.86:1, visual not confirmed.

seed_data_creation: None — used the ephemeral device identity issued on onboarding within a single browser session; MockSecurityAdapter for security calls; Gemini streaming for ask/stream.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The Higgins chip flow tests reliably in ONE playwright session (~60s per prompt because Gemini stream takes 15-20s). Sequence: goto('/') → onboarding-start-button → 'I understand' (get_by_text, no testID on privacy-disclosure accept — request adding `disclosure-accept-button`) → tab-ask → ask-input → ask-send-button → wait 20s → chips render. Onboarding step 2 (privacy disclosure) still has NO testID on its accept CTA — flagged in iter 39 as well; still not fixed. Available check screens and their run testIDs: /check → check-url-input + check-submit-button (input clears aggressively — paste then IMMEDIATELY click submit; paste-button is `check-paste-button`); /message → message-text + message-check; /device → toggles + device-save (only visible when result.status!=='protected'); /app-check → app-name + app-run; /account → identifier + account-run; /network → network-run. To verify persistence: after tapping a chip and running the check, either navigate back via `goto('/ask')` (tab-ask may be off-screen if the check screen hides the tab bar) or use `page.go_back()`. Storage key for completion is `apollo.checks.completed.v1` (JSON blob mapping CheckId → ISO timestamp) — inspect via `localStorage.getItem('apollo.checks.completed.v1')`. To force a barking result on /check, mock URL patterns to try: `https://phishing.apollo.test/login` did not bark in this session — request main agent to document which mock URLs bark on web-preview. The console warning about unique keys is present but not blocking — safe to ignore during test flow but should be filed. All contrast math done here uses WCAG relative-luminance on the composited backdrop (rgba tint over white card) and matches the numbers reported in iter 39.
rca_of_issue: Two independent misses in the iteration-40 change set. (1) markCheckDone was added to 4/6 check screens but message.tsx and check.tsx were skipped — likely because they predate the completion API and the change was made screen-by-screen; the fix is 2 one-liners mirroring device.tsx L56. (2) HigginsSpeakButton is a bespoke Pressable that predates the Button component; when the secondary-button token pair was retuned in ui.tsx L116, this component wasn't touched because it never used the Button primitive. Its style `bg: c.surfaceTertiary + border: c.border` produces a light-blue button on the sky-blue page — barely distinguishable, exactly the visual regression the request set out to fix. Fix is 2 token swaps in HigginsSpeakButton.tsx L12. Both issues are surface-level and low-risk; no theme changes needed.
